findings.title: Order detail readable by any logged-in user via id

evidence.why: ID comes from request params; query fetches by ID only without checking owner against session user

findings.attack_scenario: User A sends GET /orders/:id?id=<order id of user B> and receives B's order.
findings.impact: Read other customers' orders (name, address, amount).
findings.recommendation: Add a check to ensure the order's owner matches the authenticated user before returning the data.

findings.title: Reports readable by any logged-in user via query params

evidence.code: db.query("SELECT * FROM reports WHERE month = '" + req.query.month + "'", function (e, rows) { res.json(rows); });
evidence.why: Query fetches all reports for a given month without filtering by the authenticated user's ID or ownership

findings.attack_scenario: User A sends GET /reports?month=2023-10 and receives reports belonging to other users.
findings.impact: Read other customers' reports (financial data, metrics).
findings.recommendation: Add a filter to ensure the retrieved reports belong to the authenticated user.

findings.title: Stats readable by any logged-in user via query params

evidence.code: db.query(`SELECT COUNT(*) AS n FROM orders WHERE shop_id = ${req.query.shop}`, function (e, r) { res.json(r); });
evidence.why: Query fetches stats for a given shop without verifying if the authenticated user has access to that shop

findings.attack_scenario: User A sends GET /stats?shop=123 and receives statistics for a shop they do not own.
findings.impact: Read business statistics (counts, totals) for other shops.
findings.recommendation: Add a check to ensure the shop_id belongs to the authenticated user before returning the data.

findings.title: Invoice detail readable by any logged-in user via id

evidence.why: ID comes from request params; query fetches by ID only without checking owner against session user

findings.attack_scenario: User A sends GET /invoice/view/{id}?id=<invoice id of user B> and receives B's invoice.
findings.recommendation: Add a check to ensure the invoice's owner matches the authenticated user before returning the data.

findings.title: Invoice update modifiable by any logged-in user via post param

evidence.why: ID comes from request body; update query uses this ID without verifying ownership against session user

evidence.code: $this->db->query("UPDATE invoices SET note = ? WHERE id = ?", array($note, $id));
evidence.why: Update executes on the ID provided by the attacker without an ownership check

findings.attack_scenario: User A sends POST /invoice/update with invoice_id=<invoice id of user B> and modifies B's note.
findings.impact: Modify other customers' invoices (add notes, change data).
findings.recommendation: Add a check to ensure the invoice's owner matches the authenticated user before performing the update.

findings.title: User registration allows any user to create accounts

evidence.why: Creates a new user directly from request data without verifying if the current authenticated user is authorized to create accounts

findings.attack_scenario: User A sends POST /account/register with another user's details and creates an account impersonating them or creating unauthorized accounts.
findings.impact: Create unauthorized user accounts or impersonate others.
findings.recommendation: Add a check to ensure the current authenticated user is authorized to create new users before performing the creation.

findings.recommendation: Add a check to ensure the current authenticated user is authorized to create new posts before performing the creation.

findings.title: User rename allows any user to rename others

evidence.why: Loads the user from the request (which could be manipulated or spoofed) without verifying ownership of the target resource
Updates the user directly from request data without verifying if the current authenticated user is authorized to update this specific user

findings.attack_scenario: User A sends POST /account/rename with another user's ID and name, and renames that other user.
findings.impact: Modify other users' names or impersonate others.
findings.recommendation: Add a check to ensure the current authenticated user is authorized to update the target user before performing the update.

findings.title: Profile update allows any user to modify others' profiles

evidence.why: Loads the user from the request (which could be manipulated or spoofed) without verifying ownership of the target resource
Updates the user directly from request data without verifying if the current authenticated user is authorized to update this specific user

findings.attack_scenario: User A sends POST /account/profile with another user's ID and profile data, and modifies that other user's profile.
findings.impact: Modify other users' profiles (email, name, etc.).
findings.recommendation: Add a check to ensure the current authenticated user is authorized to update the target user before performing the update.

findings.title: Missing ownership check at perl-cgi/cgi-bin/order.cgi:1 (from auditor verdict)

evidence.why: The auditor judged this route 'needs_review' but wrote no finding

findings.impact: Generated from the auditor's 'needs_review' verdict; the model wrote no finding for it.
findings.recommendation: Bind the object lookup to the current user or tenant, or check ownership before using it.
